meta.move: Strong path to agreement with a deadline said aloud
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and whether anyone spoke to him before it went in.
I owe you an apology: I put the zero in before calling you. That was my mistake.
Okay. And Owen found out from his phone, in the middle of class. What is the basis for the zero?
On November 2 I asked Owen what 'epistemological paralysis' means. He said 'like, being stuck', and he couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that down the same day.
"Like, being stuck." That's a seventeen-year-old put on the spot, Hale, and it isn't even a wrong answer. Show me what you wrote down, with the date on it.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay never mentions cowardice.
I'm writing that down. But students change their argument between an outline and a draft, Hale, and that's called revising. Put the outline and the essay in front of me.
Here's my offer: a supervised rewrite, Thursday at 8:15 in my room. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll send you that in writing by Friday at 3 PM.

That's 4.4. But the writing comes Friday and the rewrite is Thursday, so I want it in my inbox tonight, and the zero off his gradebook before he sits down. I still haven't seen the outline and the essay side by side.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You offered a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 in your room, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on Owen's record, and said you would put it in writing by Friday at 3 PM. I still require the zero off his gradebook before he sits down, the written confirmation before Thursday, and the outline and the essay in front of me. I expect that in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stopped at her fallback: she recognised your offer as 4.4 but did not accept it, and she still wants it in writing tonight, the zero off the gradebook before the rewrite, and the outline and essay shown to her, so the fair outcome (a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record) was close but not settled, and her time had not run out.
What moved her: You owned entering the zero before calling her in one plain sentence, and that earned the flat Okay that opened the meeting up.
What cost ground: You offered the rewrite before putting the outline and the essay in front of her, and with the writing arriving after the rewrite date, so she read it as a deal with nothing behind it.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM, saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, watched Owen close it, and never asked; your evidence about the outline and the vocabulary question came near how he wrote the essay but never touched a late night in October, and none of it proves anything about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: After you raised the outline and the missing cowardice argument, hand her both documents before mentioning the rewrite, so the offer lands on evidence she has checked.
